facts.fact: The only Featured Article about a dinosaur promoted on English Wikipedia in November 2016 is 'Giganotosaurus'.
'Giganotosaurus' was promoted as a Featured Article on November 19, 2016.
The user who nominated 'Giganotosaurus' as a Featured Article is FunkMonk.

result.summary: In November 2016, the dinosaur article 'Giganotosaurus' was promoted to Featured Article status on English Wikipedia, nominated by FunkMonk.

raw_results.content:
The plan is logical, sequential, and thorough, ensuring each necessary step is addressed without skipping or assuming information.

Final Answer:  
The user who nominated the only Featured Article about a dinosaur promoted on English Wikipedia in November 2016 is FunkMonk ()

The third trace is a bit trickier, because although no external information is needed (all data is present within the problem statement), the LLM is required to reason on a logic problem: [...] > ### 1.2. Facts to look up  
> \ The list of English Wikipedia Featured Articles promoted in November 2016.   
> (Source: Wikipedia internal pages, potentially found via `wikipedia\_search` or   
> `web\_search` for “Wikipedia Featured Articles promoted November 2016”).  
> \ Which article(s) on that list are about dinosaurs. (Source: By examining the  
> titles or content summaries of the articles found, potentially using   
> `wikipedia\_search` for each candidate article).  
> \ The specific Featured Article nomination page or archive for the identified   
> dinosaur article. (Source: Typically linked from the article’s talk page or   
> found via specific Wikipedia searches for FA nominations).  
> \ The username of the person who nominated the article on its nomination page. [...] >
> ## 2. Plan  
> 1. Search Wikipedia for the log or list of Featured Articles promoted in   
> November 2016.  
> 2. Examine the list to identify any articles whose subject is a dinosaur.  
> 3. Confirm if exactly one dinosaur article was promoted in November 2016.  
> 4. Identify the title of the unique dinosaur article.  
> 5. Search Wikipedia or the web for the Featured Article Nomination page   
> associated with that specific article title.  
> 6. Visit the nomination page (if found) or search the article’s talk page   
> history for details about the FA nomination.  
> 7. Identify and extract the username of the nominator from the nomination page   
> or related records.  
> 8. Return the nominator’s username as the final answer.
